title: Node.js 24 is the minimum supported version as of v6.0.0
content:
v6.0.0 opens its Breaking Changes section with the runtime floor:

> **Node.js 24 is now the minimum supported version.**

```bash
node --version          # must be >= 24.0.0
nvm install 24 && nvm use 24
```

It is a hard requirement, not a recommendation, and it is the first thing to check when a v6 project fails in an unexplained way during install or codegen. The tutorial track agrees: the Manual Todo tutorial's prerequisites list "Node.js 24 and a package manager (pnpm or npm) installed" rather than any earlier range.

Worth pairing this with the other toolchain shifts in the same release, because they land together and a stale Node is often not the only thing lagging: `tsdown` replaced the previous build toolchain across `analytics-engine`, `builder-tools`, `ph-cli`, `ph-cmd`, `registry`, `shared` and `design-system`; processors now publish distinct `node` and `browser` entrypoints; and `sideEffects: false` was added to generated package boilerplate with pglite, jszip and renown crypto lazy-loaded.

Also from the same release: `ph-cmd` now delegates `init` and all forwarded commands to the versioned `ph-cli` binary, so version pinning finally works correctly — which means "which Node am I on" and "which ph-cli am I actually running" are now two separate questions worth asking independently.

Provenance: academy `ReleaseNotes/v6.0.0.md:182` (Breaking Changes) and `03-Build/01-ManualTodoTutorial/01-CreateNewPowerhouseProject.md:24` (Prerequisites), academy 6.2.2-dev.45.
description: v6.0.0 raised the floor to Node >= 24.0.0 as a hard breaking change, and the tutorial prerequisites now list Node.js 24 rather than a range.
